title: Spain's World Cup heroes celebrate with victory parade through Madrid
facts: Approximately one million fans attended the Spanish national football team's World Cup victory parade in Madrid.
The Spanish victory parade traveled along Madrid's central avenues toward Cibeles square.
King Felipe VI and the Spanish royal family officially received the Spanish team upon their return from the United States.
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez hosted the national team at the Moncloa palace.
Spain defeated Argentina 1-0 in extra time in New Jersey to win their second men's World Cup title.
Ferran Torres scored the decisive extra-time goal in the final against Argentina.
Spain's previous men's World Cup victory occurred in 2010 in South Africa.
Spain captain Rodri plays club football for Manchester City.
A 13-year-old boy died in Ciudad Rodrigo when a fountain collapsed during World Cup celebrations.
Spain's women's national football team won the FIFA Women's World Cup in 2023.
Spain will co-host the 2030 FIFA World Cup alongside Portugal and Morocco.
Spain defeated France in the semifinals of the 2026 World Cup tournament.
Spanish sports newspaper Marca published an article celebrating the team's victory under the headline 'The kings of all-time!'.
Lionel Messi stated on Instagram that the emotional pain from the final defeat would be hard to heal.
Andres Iniesta scored Spain's extra-time winning goal against the Netherlands in the 2010 World Cup final.
